provenance.paper_title: TAMEing Long Contexts in Personalization: Towards Training-Free and State-Aware MLLM Personalized Assistant

evidence.paraphrase: Dynamic State and Static Personalized memories store concept-aligned transient and persistent attributes.
Stable attributes migrate to static memory. For TAME, this specifically supports migration between memory tiers of dynamic and static concept attributes.
The bounded dynamic tier removes outdated attributes. For TAME, this specifically supports explicit deletion or eviction of stored items of dynamic and static concept attributes.

A frozen multimodal language model chooses Add, Modify, or Remove actions over concept attributes. For TAME, this specifically supports LLM-mediated memory editing of dynamic and static concept attributes.

The same fixed manager compares incoming concept evidence with stored attributes and resolves inconsistent or outdated entries through Modify or Remove. For TAME, this specifically supports LLM-based resolution of conflicting records of dynamic and static concept attributes.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 2): During inference, the operative memory component (dynamic and static concept attributes) changes through migration between memory tiers, explicit deletion or eviction of stored items, LLM-mediated memory editing, LLM-based resolution of conflicting records; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
